day_shape: 66 items: tanker struck in Strait of Hormuz (UKMTO report, IRGC claims sea-mine hit), Trump confirms Vance letter to Iran (characterised as medical-supplies outreach), Israeli soldier charged with Iran-paid espionage, heavy regime denials cycle; nothing from UK Parliament or OFAC.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz tanker incident
threads.summary: UKMTO reported a tanker struck by an unidentified projectile after transiting the Strait of Hormuz, relayed by Iranian outlets as a missile strike. Iran's Army Public Relations claimed the vessel was a 'violating tanker' that hit sea mines in a prohibited area, and the IRGC denied a CENTCOM statement that commercial ships had not encountered mines.

threads.label: Vance letter to Tehran
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post and Iran International reported Tehran received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance but has not responded; Trump said the outreach concerned medical supplies, disputing reports it sought to revive negotiations. Iranian security sources confirmed receipt of a Vance message to Major-General Mohsen Rezaei, while IRIB commentators and Speaker Ghalibaf said Iran's seven conditions remain the only basis for progress.

threads.label: Iran war footing and US posture
threads.summary: Iran International reported Washington is weighing a week-long military campaign against Tehran after US midterms, while Iranian media debated prospects of another war and Reuters found Iran imported at least $2 billion in military supplies via 5,000 agencies since January 2025. CENTCOM posted imagery of a US F-16 over the Middle East, and CNN reported Somali piracy at its highest level since 2013 as US naval attention is diverted.

threads.label: Iran-linked security cases abroad
threads.summary: An Israeli soldier was arrested and charged with espionage tasks for Iran in exchange for cryptocurrency, following a September Shin Bet-led investigation. A Syrian court imposed life imprisonment in a case involving an armed group affiliated with the IRGC-linked Liwa al-Quds, and The Telegraph reported Iran is preparing to disrupt US midterm elections.

threads.label: Regional fallout: Lebanon, Yemen, Egypt
threads.summary: Four Lebanese ministers boycotted a Cabinet meeting over delays in referring Hezbollah's explosives case to the Judicial Council, and the Jerusalem Post reported Houthis still hold Jewish prisoner Levi Marhabi despite a release order. Defa Press cited Yemen's Yahya Saree claiming 116 Saudi strikes in 24 hours, and Egypt denied citizenship to Hamas negotiator Ghazi Hamad's daughter on security grounds.

threads.label: Iran reads Israeli election
threads.summary: Iran International and Jerusalem Post reported Iranian and regional debate over how Netanyahu's weakened position after Israel's election might affect policy on Iran. A Ghalibaf-linked conservative daily, Khorasan, argued Iran would benefit from his departure even without a policy shift.

threads.label: Khamenei mobilisation and regime messaging
threads.summary: Khamenei's office posted messaging on 'Patriotic Medal-Bearers' and student gatherings at Tehran University, while Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghaii said public night-square turnout backs diplomacy. IRGC Deputy Commander Izadi urged fighters 'not to abandon the fields', and Khamenei adviser Mohammad Mokhber said Europe 'sowed wind and reaps the storm' alongside the US.

events.title_en: Purjamshidian: Over 3 million Iranian pilgrims participated in the Arbaeen procession
events.summary_en: Purjamshidian: Over 3 million Iranian pilgrims participated in the Arbaeen procession. The Deputy Minister of Interior for Security and Law Enforcement said that more than 3 million and 400 thousand Iranian pilgrims travelled to Iraq this year to visit Arbaeen. The Arbaeen ceremony in the past two years has been held without security incidents through cooperation between Iran and Iraq's security and law enforcement forces. In the past, pilgrims were detained for hours at borders, but this year with cooperation between various agencies, border crossing was carried out more quickly. Passport coordination between the two countries proceeded in a way that allowed pilgrims to be checked and cross in a short time.
